note: Genuine, verified historical engine changes that an external game may need to act on when its engine dependency moves across them. This is not a log of every engine commit: entries are added only when a real game-facing effect was confirmed against this repository's history (see 'reference'). Selection in tools/upgrade.py combines since_commit (is it between the game's last verified revision and the upgrade target?) with 'detect' evidence read from the game's own source; a revision match alone is a hint, not a verdict.

migrations.title: One mouse-look convention (devkit::look); hand-rolled look from mouse_delta_position() is inverted
migrations.summary: Before this commit, macroquad's mouse_delta_position() (previous-minus-current, both axes flipped) was easy to read directly for camera look, which inverts turning and pitch. The engine's own multiplayer-game template shipped with exactly this bug and was fixed in the same commit. A custom-sim game that reads mouse_delta_position() itself for look has the same defect regardless of its engine dependency version; bumping the dependency does not fix it automatically.
migrations.repair: Replace the direct read with devkit::look::MouseLook (pixels from game_input::mouse_pixels()), or feed the same [right, down] delta into Controller::look(dx, dy, 1.0, false). Do not hand-write a yaw/pitch formula. See docs/CUSTOM_SIM_CHEATSHEET.md and docs/adr/0020-look-scale-and-dev-loop.md.
migrations.verification: No automated per-game camera regression exists in the engine. Verify manually: capture before/after frames while looking up and right and confirm the camera turns the same way the input moved (docs/HEADLESS_CAPTURE.md, --capture/--script).
migrations.limitations: Detection is a source grep for the function name; a game could reference it for an unrelated reason, which would be a false positive requiring manual review. A game that never reads this function directly (uses only Controller::look through the shared input kit) is correctly reported not_applicable even if its baseline predates since_commit.

migrations.title: Oversized/degenerate Template rendering traps closed (Template::split, Template::quad_facing)
migrations.summary: A Template batch past 65,535 vertices now splits instead of silently dropping its mesh, and quad winding is corrected to always face its normal. Both are internal to Batch::add/to_meshes; no game-facing API changed.
migrations.repair: None: applied automatically by taking the dependency update. No game-side change is needed or possible.
migrations.verification: Covered by the engine's own test suite (not re-run per game). Informational only; included so a plan does not look silent about a real rendering fix landing in scope.
migrations.limitations: No per-game evidence is checked. This record only reports presence/absence by revision range, never a confirmed effect on a specific game's geometry.

migrations.title: viewer::netplay kit available for custom simulations
migrations.summary: Games with hand-rolled client/server networking written before this commit may delete that code and adopt the shared NetGame/ClientView kit on net::codec, net::loopback and net::any. Spooky Kart's own port deleted about 1,900 lines doing this; its net tests still passed afterward.
migrations.repair: See docs/NETPLAY.md and the netplay::toy example for the target shape: rules become a NetGame, the replica/prediction become a ClientView. Keep the game's own networking tests passing before and after the port; this is an opt-in rewrite, not required for the dependency bump to work.
migrations.verification: The game's own networking tests (if any) must still pass after adoption. Engine-side guarantee: tests/netplay.rs, on an in-memory network with loss, jitter and delay.
migrations.limitations: File-presence detection only; a game may have files with these names for reasons unrelated to hand-rolled networking (false positive), or may hide its networking code under different file names (false negative). Treat as a hint requiring a quick read of the named files, not a verdict.

migrations.title: Persistent audio settings and a generated ambient-music stem are available for custom simulations
migrations.summary: Before this commit, every custom-sim game constructed SoundBank with hard-coded volumes, played no music (start_music() was always called with zero stems), and had no way for a player to turn music or sound effects off that survived a relaunch. devkit::save::Settings now has music_on/sfx_on toggles plus music_level()/sfx_level() helpers, devkit::synth::AmbientSpec/ambient_loop generates a seamless background track, and GameShell::local_menu_with_audio adds a non-breaking Settings screen (toggles plus a 'Save music' download button). A game can adopt as little as the Settings persistence or as much as the full menu screen.
migrations.repair: See docs/AUDIO.md. Minimum: load devkit::Settings at startup (beside_exe("settings.json")) and pass settings.sfx_level()/settings.music_level() into SoundBank::start instead of hard-coded volumes. Full adoption: also add a music stem from ambient_loop, call sounds.update_music every frame, and switch the pause menu to GameShell::local_menu_with_audio (local_menu keeps working unchanged if you do not).
migrations.verification: No automated per-game audio-settings regression exists in the engine; verify manually that toggling music/sound in the Settings screen takes effect immediately and that the choice survives quitting and relaunching the game (the settings.json file beside the executable).
migrations.limitations: Detection only confirms the game already uses SoundBank (true for essentially every custom-sim game); it cannot tell whether a game already hand-rolled its own equivalent of Settings persistence before this feature existed, which would be a false positive for 'nothing done yet'. Treat as a hint to check, not a verdict.

migrations.title: The Windows native key reader polls the full keyboard (R, digits and most letters were silently never pressed)
migrations.summary: Before this commit the native Windows key reader (the fn(i32) -> i16 reader a game passes to ClientInput::begin_frame_with_keyboard, usually platform::keyboard()) polled only a 23-key shortlist. Any other key, including R, the digits and most letters, never read as pressed on Windows once the reader was installed, while Linux (macroquad events) behaved correctly, so headless tests and captures could not show it. The engine now polls a full table (game_input::KEY_TABLE), and a key outside it prints once and trips a debug_assert!. Nothing in the game's source changes.
migrations.repair: None in the game's source: taking the dependency update applies it. An already-released Windows build does NOT pick it up until the game is rebuilt against the new engine revision and re-released (re-run scripts/blue ship and republish).
migrations.verification: Engine side: the game_input tests drive the table-driven path with a fake key source on Linux. A real Windows key test (press R at game over) is still the only proof of real input; python tools/be2.py check --windows only type-checks the Windows code.
migrations.limitations: No per-game evidence is checked, so this reports presence by revision range only. It cannot tell which games had a key silently dead; any game that binds R, a digit or a letter outside the old shortlist was affected.

migrations.title: ClientInput::restart_requested: one "play again" check (R, Enter or pad A/Start) instead of a hand-rolled one
migrations.summary: Games each hand-rolled restart differently (R only; R or Enter; plus a controller button), so players could not rely on one key. ClientInput::restart_requested(game_over) is true once per press of R, Enter or pad South/Start, only while the game is over and the window is focused. The custom-sim template uses it.
migrations.repair: Replace the game's own restart condition (for example `sim.over && (input.pressed(KeyCode::R) || ..)`) with `input.restart_requested(sim.over)` and keep any restart banner text saying R. Start also opens the pause menu in the shell, so check how the game behaves when both happen. See docs/CUSTOM_SIM_CHEATSHEET.md.
migrations.verification: No automated per-game regression exists; verify manually that after game over R, Enter and pad A each start a new run exactly once and that R during play does nothing. Engine side: the restart_* tests in src/viewer/game_input.rs.
migrations.limitations: A source grep for KeyCode::R, which is how nearly every hand-rolled restart is written, but R is also used for reload, rotate and other actions: a false positive needs a quick read of the match. A game that restarts on another key (or only through a menu) is a false negative. Treat it as a hint, not a verdict.
